source_title: Dante's Virus and the Guide Who Built Hell
summary: This April 8, 2026 re-upload of the Great Books Dante lecture reinforces already-public Guide Trap, Poetry, Eschatology, Free Will, and Fictional Heroes anchors rather than creating a new public concept; its value is cleaner duplicate accounting and already-linked episode provenance.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Virgil must be put on a pedestal so the reader can learn to defeat him.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The public Guide Trap page already carries the mechanism from the original upload; this re-upload's read links the same necessary-guide danger to the existing anchor.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Dialogue matters because every speaker speaks from a worldview.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The re-upload directly supports the guide-speech diagnostic already public on The Guide Who Becomes A Trap.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Virgil hears Beatrice through contract, duty, exchange, and piety.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The re-upload repeats the already-public mechanism where unconditional rescue is translated back into the guide's exchange-world.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Virgil is master of hell because the Aeneid created the emotions hell recognizes.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The re-upload reinforces the already-public claim that Virgil can guide through hell because his poetry belongs to hell's emotional grammar.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Will and desire make the soul, and people move toward hell because they think it is best for them.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The re-upload supports the Eschatology anchor for hell as trained desire rather than merely external punishment.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Hell becomes self-selected when desire and will move toward the prison.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The same passage also belongs to Free Will because Jiang makes chosen hell a consequence of will and desire, not only sacred geography.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Dante names Dido to resurrect the person Virgil's map tried not to face.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The re-upload has a direct read mark to the public Guide Trap memory-repair anchor.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: The literary guide enters the self as father and teacher while carrying a world that must be overcome.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The re-upload supports the Fictional Heroes anchor for the dangerous interior guest, but the existing public page already carries the same April 8 mechanism from the original upload.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: No ordinary public append is needed. The re-upload confirms the existing April 8 Guide Trap anchors on necessary guidance, speech revealing a world, grace translated into contract, Virgil native to hell's grammar, and memory restored against the guide's omission.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Guide Trap owns trusted mediation, Virgil's hidden world, and the guide's omissions. Poetry owns the medium of memorized language; Free Will and Eschatology own chosen hell when desire and final-order logic are primary.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use this re-upload only as duplicate reinforcement for the poetry-as-virus mechanism: poetry enters memory, creates dissonance, and remakes perception over time.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Poetry owns the civilizational medium. Guide Trap owns the specific Virgil/Dante danger where a guide's world is smuggled into rescue.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use this re-upload only as support for the existing chosen-hell anchor, where hell is a world built by piety, obedience, empire, hatred, and trained desire.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Eschatology owns hell as final-order/world-script. Free Will owns the soul-forming will and desire; Guide Trap owns the mediator whose grammar makes hell feel natural.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use the re-upload as duplicate support for chosen hell and anti-reciprocity: free will and reciprocity contradict each other, and a soul moves toward what it wants.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Free Will owns the chosen burden; Guide Trap owns Virgil's translation of grace into contract; Human Heart owns love and forgiveness when person-recognition is central.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use the re-upload as duplicate support for Virgil as dangerous interior guide: a fictional/literary person can enter the self as savior, father, and teacher while carrying a world the reader must defeat.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Fictional Heroes owns the interior-person mechanism. Guide Trap owns the mediation structure; Poetry owns the medium by which the person enters memory.

chronology_notes.note: This 2026-04-08 video is a re-upload with fixed audio of the same Great Books #9 Dante lecture already accounted under predictive-history-6m1z-v3wgok. Treat it as duplicate source support and provenance redundancy, not as a later development in Jiang's Dante chronology.

Because the original upload already generated public Guide Trap, Poetry, Eschatology, Free Will, and Fictional Heroes anchors, the re-upload should not reset origin language or create a second Dante #9 concept line.

next_actions.action: Do not create standalone Dante Virus, Guide Who Built Hell, Virgil Master Of Hell, Dido Resurrection, Poetry Virus, Chosen Hell, Minos Warning, or Free Will Versus Reciprocity pages from this re-upload alone.
If provenance work follows, compare the original upload and re-upload episode reads before linking additional marks; prefer stable public lens-point IDs over adding duplicate public prose.

If a future public synthesis touches the Dante cluster, treat this source as confirmation for the existing Guide Trap page and route any new material through the April 29 Dante hierarchy impact and later Purgatorio/Statius pressure rather than through another April 8 append.
